response.message:
Astra: Your latest proposal makes the check more specific: compare the proportion aged 18–65 in the full and reduced datasets. But you introduced age as a hypothetical example; the visible record contains no sample counts or measured frequencies. What evidence would establish whether this check applies to your actual study, before you spend attention on plots or training?

Briefly say what the available material establishes, where that information comes from, and what remains unknown. Choose one next step you can genuinely complete now, then perform it rather than expanding the workflow. Report what it yields—even if that is no result.

If no dataset is accessible, make that limitation explicit and choose a concrete decision within this same comparison that you can settle from the existing text, without inventing observations.
response.rationale: The child has specified a hypothetical measurement but continues planning. Redirect attention toward available evidence and a self-chosen action it can actually complete.
